title: Signal Groups
outro_say: Next: turning Groups into a decision, with Signal Sets.

steps.screen: The diagram with Signal Groups lit, then the Group editor
steps.say: A Signal Group turns several signals into one reading: | a score from minus one hundred to plus one hundred, and a label, such as Bullish.

steps.screen: "Start from": the starter Groups listed; then "New Group"
steps.say: You can start from a starter Group, the same ones behind the dashboard's pre-configured Trend, Stretch and Flow, | or from scratch. Let's build our own.

steps.screen: Tapping + on Moving averages, Ichimoku cloud and MACD line; three cards appear
steps.say: Add signals by dragging them in, or tapping plus. | Here: moving averages, the Ichimoku cloud, and the MACD line.
Each signal has a role. Score signals are combined into the Group's score. | Condition signals are only used in rules, and Context is shown alongside.

steps.screen: Adding a rule: score at least +30 → Bullish; then at most -30 → Bearish; "Otherwise: Neutral"
steps.say: Rules give the labels, checked from the top: the first that matches wins. | At least plus thirty is Bullish. At most minus thirty is Bearish. Otherwise, Neutral.

steps.screen: The rule panel's note about Unknown
steps.say: If a rule can't be checked because a reading is missing, the label is Unknown, | never a guess.

steps.screen: Adding Regime evidence as a Condition, then + Veto: "Daily regime is ranging"
steps.say: Vetoes protect you from the wrong conditions. | Here, if the daily market is ranging, every label becomes Vetoed.

steps.screen: The Checks panel turns green; the automatic description
steps.say: The checks tell you what blocks saving, and what is only a warning. | And the description is written for you, in plain words.

steps.screen: Naming it "My Trend" and pressing Save as a new Group
steps.say: Name it, and save. It's yours, and private, until you publish it. | Changing it later saves a new version, so earlier ones stay as they were.

steps.screen: Summary card: one score, your labels, your veto
steps.say: Why it helps: your reading of the trend, | the same every time, on every asset.
